Sara / Sergio —

Sorry for the delay — attached is a quick CSV (redwood-billing-example.csv) that shows three rows:
A) Per-token billing (raw tokens, token rate, billable amount)
B) Session-unit aggregation (session-unit size = 3,000 tokens, sessions counted and rounded up to nearest whole unit)
C) Blended example (embeddings line + chat line) with the early-commit credit spread equally across 12 months.

Summary of what you should expect from the math:
- Session-unit aggregation reduces invoice line-item noise but can increase billed units if your average session is small (< 3,000 tokens) because we round up each session to the unit size.
- Blended vs separate lines does not change total spend if you keep raw token rates identical; it just changes how charges are presented.
- The early-commit credit is applied as a monthly credit equal to (commit_discount * committed_monthly_spend) / 12. For GLR example: 15% discount on a $100k monthly baseline -> $15k annual credit -> $1,250 monthly credit.

Concrete worked example (from CSV):
- Raw tokens (month): 18,350,000 tokens -> per-token billing at $0.0008 = $14,680.
- Session-unit aggregation: 6,200 sessions (round up each session) -> session-unit price equivalent to token-rate * unit-size -> billed amount = $15,600 (difference due to rounding).
- After early-commit credit applied monthly: Per-token line -> $14,680 - $1,250 = $13,430; Session-unit line -> $15,600 - $1,250 = $14,350.

Attachments included: redwood-billing-example.csv (worked numbers) and a short PDF that maps the slab tiers to invoice line names.

If this looks good I can produce a one-page SOW-friendly clause showing the exact proration language (how we round partial months and how we apply the credit if they churn early).
